tasks.title: Bird Migration
tasks.transcript: Listen to a talk in a science class. Let's talk about bird migration. Migratory birds travel vast distances between their breeding and wintering grounds, often covering thousands of miles. These journeys are driven by the need to find suitable habitats with abundant food supplies and favorable climate conditions. One of the most remarkable aspects of migration is the ability to navigate accurately over such distances. Birds use a variety of navigational cues, such as the position of the sun, stars, and, interestingly, Earth's magnetic field. Certain bird species have a special protein in their eyes that allows them to sense magnetic fields, and this helps them stay on course. Migration is not without risk. Disease, predators, starvation, and storms all take a toll. Different degrees of habitat destruction, light pollution, and climate change have kept a number of migrating species from completing their journeys. A decrease in the population of migrating birds may cause an imbalance in food webs. One practical step people can take is turning off unnecessary lights at night during peak migration seasons. Friendly building design and programs that encourage turning off unnecessary lighting during peak migration seasons can help more birds arrive safely.
